summary: Eight comment-endorsed finds spanning C development, backups, accounting, satellite imagery, paper airplanes, and systems learning.
telegram_footer: 8 items surfaced | 30/30 /front stories processed, 4,983 comments | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Clay
items.source_story_title: CUI – Native UI components for C
items.summary: C UI layout library praised for its engineering in a native-interface discussion.
items.why_included: A named alternative receives explicit praise rather than a bare comparison.
items.evidence: A commenter promotes Clay as a beautiful piece of engineering.

evidence_sources.author: mllev15
evidence_sources.excerpt: I will now use this opportunity to promote Clay (not mine obviously), which is absolutely loaded with heart and soul, and is a beautiful piece of engineering:

items.name: WPE WebKit
items.source_story_title: Zebkit – Chromium as an embeddable library
items.summary: Embedded web engine recommended for lighter deployments; developer experience and compatibility have trade-offs.
items.why_included: The recommendation names a practical Chromium alternative and states when it fits.
items.evidence: A commenter calls WPE WebKit a worthwhile lightweight Chrome/CEF alternative when content can be tailored, while noting worse developer experience and web compatibility.

evidence_sources.author: torginus
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's a fairly significantly more lightweight option to Chrome/CEF, that does suffer from a somewhat worse DX and compat with web content, but if you can tailor your content to it, rather than looking for a flawless ootb experience, it's a worthwhile choice.

items.name: Kopia
items.source_story_title: Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators
items.summary: Encrypted backup software used for scheduled offsite backups with client-side encryption.
items.why_included: A first-hand workflow supplies a concrete alternative to trusting cloud providers with plaintext.
items.evidence: A commenter uses Kopia to encrypt and schedule offsite backups to MEGA, describing the resulting setup as well encrypted.

evidence_sources.author: mapontosevenths
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Kopia to perform (and encrypt) the backups, so they never get anything other than the raw data and it's all done on a schedule.

items.name: FreeAgent
items.summary: Small-business accounting software endorsed by a former self-employed UK user.
items.why_included: Direct positive first-hand experience stands out in a thread about software price increases.
items.evidence: A former self-employed UK user says FreeAgent worked very well.

evidence_sources.author: gadders
evidence_sources.excerpt: When I was self-employed in the UK, I used Freeagent which worked very well.

items.name: Watched.earth
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Every satellite that passed over any place this week, and its photos
items.summary: Satellite imagery explorer praised for easy access and usefulness when planning backpacking trips.
items.why_included: Independent comments endorse both practical usefulness and interface quality.
items.evidence: One commenter praises backpacking-trip planning and easier access than Copernicus; another praises the interface while linking a San Francisco Bay image.

evidence_sources.author: wnissen
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is great for planning backpacking trips. I have been using Copernicus but you have a lot more and it's much easier to access. Very nice!

evidence_sources.author: creeble
evidence_sources.excerpt: Um, wow. Amazing UI. This photo of the SF Bay this morning is a great representation of the fog that settles in over the area:

items.name: Mystic paper airplane
items.source_story_title: Foldable Flight: The Best Paper Airplanes
items.summary: Quick A4 paper-airplane tutorial; commenters folded it and praised its smooth flight.
items.why_included: Two hands-on reports make this a low-friction family experiment, not just a nostalgic mention.
items.evidence: A commenter follows the A4 tutorial and calls the result their best-performing paper airplane; a reply reports making one and praises its smooth flight.

evidence_sources.author: literallyanythi
evidence_sources.excerpt: As someone who only knew the "naive" way to make paper airplanes from A4 paper, this is the best performing and prettiest paper airplane I've made in my life!

evidence_sources.author: andai
evidence_sources.excerpt: Wow, just made one. She flies very smooth!

items.name: Harvard CS61
items.summary: Systems-programming course recommended for learning memory allocation and related low-level topics.
items.why_included: An explicit learning-resource recommendation offers a deeper path beyond the submitted article.
items.evidence: A commenter links the 2026 CS61 course and calls it a good learning resource for malloc and related topics.

evidence_sources.author: projectileboy

items.summary: Classic Phrack article on malloc internals and exploitation, explicitly recommended in the comments.

items.evidence: A commenter highly recommends Michel Kaempf's 2001 Phrack article Vudo malloc tricks.
